question: Does the best P0572 setting that descriptively improved both development and holdout means transfer to the three P0567 pilot cluster maps?

locked_formula.activation: A=sqrt(1-C)*B_T with p=2, 50 kpc field softening, and F160W weight power one
locked_formula.selection_history: Among the 14 post-hoc P0572 candidates that improved both the seven-system development mean and three-system holdout mean versus local, this candidate had the lowest development JS. It was locked before any P0572B pilot map score.

data.primary_target: mean of 100 Lenstool convergence realizations with the P0567 background subtraction, positive clipping, smoothing, and normalization
data.uncertainty: score locked and local predictions against all 100 maps per system
data.independence_limit: These systems are globally spent and their P0567 peak locations entered P0571B pilot validation. P0572B is a forward-map replication stress test, not untouched validation.

cross_domain.galaxy: exact angular null in the net axisymmetric limit; no SPARC rotation change
cross_domain.solar: exact one-source null; no Solar or Mercury change

claim_limits: The lens targets are standard-GR normalized convergence maps, not raw observables or absolute lens strength.
The source catalogs omit gas, ICL, and resolved stellar mass-to-light variation.
The locked setting was selected post-hoc from P0572's spent development and holdout aggregates.
P0571B already inspected peak locations in these same pilot lens maps.
Even a pass would authorize only a future fresh-sample and raw-lensing test, not a theory claim.
